description: Any window from your Mac, live on your iPhone or iPad. Touch, Apple Pencil, trackpad and keys. Free, open source, no servers.

latest_release.name: Sill 0.6.2
latest_release.body:
Sill 0.6.2 hides its controls when you want only the picture, keeps your Mac's picture playing in Picture in Picture when you leave the app, and steps the Desktop button through a Mac's screens. Sill for Mac can now update itself. It also shows its version where you can find it, and fixes where a window goes back to on a Mac with more than one screen.

**One version for both apps.** This is Sill for Mac 0.6.2 (1612), and it goes with Sill for iPhone and iPad 0.6.2 (1607), built from the same app code (commit aea3547, which differs from this release's only in words). Sill for iPhone and iPad 0.6.2 is on the App Store. Each half works with the other's 0.6.1. Stepping through a Mac's screens needs 0.6.2 on both.

**New for the iPhone and iPad**
- **Full screen.** Settings › Full Screen hides all of Sill's controls, so the Mac's picture gets the screen. Swipe in from the left edge to bring them back, or shake your iPhone or iPad (Shake to Show Controls, on unless you turn it off). While the controls are hidden, a drag that starts at the left edge and goes right brings them back and doesn't reach the Mac (#279, #92, #280).
- **Picture in Picture.** Turn on Picture in Picture in Settings › This iPad (or This iPhone), and the Mac's picture keeps playing in iOS's Picture in Picture window when you leave Sill, with the Mac's sound if Send Audio is on. It is for watching: nothing you tap there reaches the Mac. Off unless you turn it on, and iOS's own Start PiP Automatically must be on (#291).
- **The Desktop button steps through your Mac's screens.** On a Mac with more than one screen, each tap on Desktop shows the next one, the main screen first, and the button says which one is up. Needs Sill for Mac 0.6.2 (#91, #139; built on a pull request by addhumal).
- **The version, where you can find it.** "Sill 0.6.2 (1607)" is at the bottom of the connect screen and at the end of Settings. Touch and hold it to copy it for a bug report.
- **A Mac you reach over a VPN stays reachable** when the VPN was off on the Mac for a while. Sill used to forget the Mac's VPN addresses the first time the Mac listed none; it now keeps them for 90 days.
- **Settings › Quality** shows the quality's name alone, so the row stays on one line on an iPhone on its side. The menu still lists each quality with its rate. (iOS 18 and later.)

**New for the Mac**
- **Sill for Mac updates itself.** When a newer release is out, Settings › General has **Update Now**: it downloads the release from GitHub, checks it two ways (Apple's signature and notarization for Sill's developer, and Sill's own update key), puts it in place of the copy you have and restarts Sill. **Automatically update Sill**, off unless you turn it on, does the same by itself two days after Sill first finds a release, once no device has been connected for 5 minutes. It never disconnects anyone. This starts with the release after this one: 0.6.2 is the first Sill that can update itself, so 0.6.1 and earlier still get 0.6.2 by downloading it.
- **Use nightly builds**, in Settings › General, off unless you turn it on. Sill then also offers each night's build, which GitHub builds and signs from Sill's newest code with nobody looking at it first. A nightly installs only when you click Update Now; Automatically update Sill installs releases only. Someone on a nightly is offered the release it led up to once that is out.
- **A window goes back where it was.** With Virtual Display on and more than one screen, a window you had streamed came back on the main screen. It now returns to the screen, size and place it had.
- **The Desktop's screens**, for the Desktop button above: Sill lists your Mac's screens, the main one first, and sends the one your device steps to.
- **Away from home through a relay on the Mac.** A device that reaches Sill through something on the Mac that relays it, such as a userspace Tailscale or WireGuard node, an SSH tunnel or a proxy, now counts as away from home and gets the away quality (#32

detail.readme:
# Sill

Any window from your Mac, on your iPhone and iPad.

Sill shows a window from your Mac, or the whole desktop, on your iPhone or
iPad. You use it there with touch, a trackpad, a keyboard or Apple Pencil.
Sill for Mac captures the window, encodes it as HEVC video and sends it to the
Sill app on your device. Your taps, clicks, scrolls and keys go back to your
Mac. Your Mac and your device connect on the same network, over a USB cable,
with Direct Wireless Connection when they share no network, or through your
own VPN, such as Tailscale, with Remote Access. There is no account and no
server in between.

**[getsill.app](https://getsill.app)** ·
[Download for Mac](https://getsill.app/download) ·
[Support](https://getsill.app/support) ·
[Privacy](https://getsill.app/privacy) ·
[Terms](https://getsill.app/terms)

[![CI](https://github.com/Saffsanity/sill/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/Saffsanity/sill/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

[![Download on the App Store](https://tools.applemediaservices.com/api/badges/download-on-the-app-store/black/en-us?size=250x83)](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6816359860)

Sill for Mac is a free, notarized download from
[getsill.app](https://getsill.app/download); with [Homebrew](https://brew.sh),
`brew install --cask saffsanity/sill/sill` installs the same download from
Sill's own [tap](https://github.com/Saffsanity/homebrew-sill). Sill for iPhone
and iPad is free on the [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6816359860),
and you can also build it from source (below).

From 0.6.2 on, Sill for Mac updates itself from Settings › General with Update Now, or by
itself when you turn on Automatically update Sill (off unless you do; it installs
only while no iPhone or iPad is connected). Either way it checks a new version two
ways before installing it: Apple's signature and notarization for Sill's
developer, and the release signed with Sill's own update key.

To try the next version before it ships: Sill for iPhone and iPad has a
[public beta on TestFlight](https://testflight.apple.com/join/6v7nqyn3), and Sill for Mac
has [nightly builds](https://github.com/Saffsanity/sill/releases/tag/nightly) on
GitHub, notarized like a release but not supported. Your devices stay paired
(a nightly uses the release's identity). Sill offers a nightly as an update only
with Use nightly builds on: otherwise the release above is the one to use.

## Screenshots

These are the iPad screenshots from the App Store; on iPhone and iPhone Duo,
Sill has layouts of its own.

| [!["Your Mac, on your iPad." The Mac's Weather app on an iPad held sideways, under Sill's bar of window thumbnails and buttons.](design/screenshots/ipad-1.jpg)](design/screenshots/ipad-1.jpg) | [!["Laptop mode." An iPad held upright, with the Mac's Clock app on top and Sill's bar, a row of keys and a trackpad below it.](design/screenshots/ipad-2.jpg)](design/screenshots/ipad-2.jpg) | [!["Sharp and smooth." Sill's Settings panel on an iPad held upright, with the Mac's Quality, Resolution and Frame Rate settings.](design/screenshots/ipad-3.jpg)](design/screenshots/ipad-3.jpg) |
| :---: | :---: | :---: |
| [!["Pair once. Private always." Sill's Connect to a Mac screen on an iPad, with a Mac listed as Wired and Add a Mac below it.](design/screenshots/ipad-4.jpg)](design/screenshots/ipad-4.jpg) | [!["Launch any Mac app." Sill's Apps list on an iPad held sideways, with a search field, the apps open now and every app installed on the Mac.](design/screenshots/ipad-5.jpg)](design/screenshots/ipad-5.jpg) | [!["Every window, one tap away." On an iPad held sideways, a window's thumbnail held in Sill's bar shows Close, Minimize and Full Screen.](design/screenshots/ipad-6.jpg)](design/screenshots/ipad-6.jpg) |

## Requirements

- A Mac with Apple silicon or an Intel processor, on macOS 14 or later.
- An iPhone or iPad with iOS 17 or iPadOS 17 or later.
- On your Mac, Sill asks for Screen Recording, to show your windows, and
  Accessibility, to click, scroll and type for you and to move and size the
  window it shows. On macOS 15 or later, also allow Local Network. On your
  iPhone or iPad, Sill asks for Local Network, to find your Mac, and for the
  camera when you scan your Mac's pairing code (you can type the code
  instead).
- Your Mac and your device on the same network, joined by a USB cable, or near
  each other with Direct Wireless Connection on. Away from home, your own VPN,
  such as Tailscale, with Remote Access on.

## How it works

- **Sill for Mac** lives in the menu bar. When your device picks a window, or
  the whole desktop, Sill captures it with ScreenCaptureKit and encodes it as
  HEVC with VideoToolbox, on the hardware video encoder in your Mac (or, while
  that is busy, in software). It captures nothing while no device is connected.
- **The picture** goes over an encrypted connection (TLS 1.3) straight to the
  Sill app on your iPhone or iPad, which decodes and shows it. When the
  encoder or the link falls behind, Sill drops frames rather than queue them,
  so the picture stays current.
- **Your input** goes back the same way: taps and clicks, scrolls with
  momentum, the on-screen trackpad, keys and typed text, and Apple Pencil as
  the pointer. Sill for Mac turns it into mouse and keyboard events, which
  needs Accessibility. A keyboard attached to your device types on your Mac as
  soon as the picture shows, Esc included, and a trackpad or a mouse scrolls
  the window under its pointer. Chinese, Japanese, Korean and other languages
  whose input methods compose text are typed with the keyboards you set up on
  your device: you compose and choose there, and what you choose is typed on
  your Mac. Dictation types on your Mac too. Reverse Scrolling, in the settings
  panel, turns a finger's scroll and the on-screen trackpad's the other way.
  Three fingers swipe and pinch as on a Mac's trackpad: Mission Control, App
  Exposé, the Spaces, Apps and Show Desktop, through the keyboard shortcuts
  your Mac has for them.
  Pinch the picture to zoom it, up to 5×, around the point between your
  fingers; two fingers move a zoomed picture, and a pinch all the way out
  shows the whole picture again.
- **On iPhone**, held upright, the picture is on top with buttons, keys and a
  trackpad below. Larger Picture, in the settings panel, gives a window's
  picture the room of the window thumbnails, down to where the keyboard comes
  up; the Desktop keeps the usual layout. With the virtual display (on unless
  you turn it off in Sill for Mac), your Mac makes a window fill the taller
  picture; with it off, once you set the window's text size with Aa.
- **The clipboard** goes both ways while Share Clipboard is on, in both apps:
  text you copy on your Mac is ready to paste on your device, and Paste in
  Sill pastes what you copied on your device where your Mac's cursor is (with
  Paste on … Right Away off, it only goes to your Mac's clipboard, where you
  press ⌘V). Sill never reads your device's clipboard by itself.
- **Sound from your Mac** is a beta, on by default; Send Audio (Beta) in the
  Sill menu or Sill's Settings on your Mac, or in the settings panel of Sill on
  your iPhone or iPad, turns it off and on. Sill for Mac captures the sound of
  the window's app, or of every app for the Desktop, and every connected device
  plays it a moment behind the picture, never ahead of it. Your Mac keeps
  playing it too, and Mute in a device's settings panel silences it on that
  device alone.
- **On iPhone Duo**, Sill follows the hinge: open it flat and your Mac fills
  the inner display; half open, the picture is above the fold with a trackpad
  and keys below; closed, Sill runs on the cover display. Nothing you touch
  sits on the fold.
- **The Desktop** on a Mac with more than one screen: tap Desktop while it
  shows to step to the next screen, starting from your main one. The button
  shows which screen is up.
- **The menus** of the app you use reach your device too: in the iPad's own
  menu bar on iPadOS 26 or later, and behind the Menus button in Sill's bar.
  Sill for Mac reads each menu from the app as you open it and chooses the
  item you pick, through Accessibility. When someone moves the mouse at your
  Mac, your device shows the pointer where it is.
- **The connect screen** on your device shows each Mac as a tile, a paired Mac
  with its screen as your last session with it ended. The picture stays on
  your device until you remove it or forget the Mac. The button beside
  "Connect to a Mac" lists them instead, and Sill remembers which you chose.
- **A short tour** shows Sill's controls the first time your device shows a
  Mac's picture, and once more after an update that adds controls, with
  what's new marked New; Take the Tour, in the settings panel, shows it again.
- **Nearby**, your device finds your Mac with Bonjour on your local network.
  Over a USB cable, your Mac shows as Wired and the connection uses the cable.
  With no shared network, Direct Wireless Connection (off by default) connects
  over peer-to-peer Wi-Fi, the way AirDrop does.
- **Pairing**: you pair each iPhone or iPad with your Mac once. Tap your Mac on
  the device, and your Mac shows a code: scan it, or type its 12 digits. Over
  a USB cable the device pairs by itself. From then on each end knows the
  other's key, and every connection, nearby or away, is pinned to those keys.
  In Sill's Settings on your Mac, Devices lists the devices you paired, and
  you can remove any of them there. If you use your Mac through Screen Sharing
  or another remote desktop app, as you would a Mac without a display, Sill's
  pairing window doesn't show there until you turn on Show the pairing window
  to screen sharing in the same place. It is off by default: while it is on,
  anyone who can see your Mac's screen remotely can read the code.
- **Away from home**, Remote Access (off by default) lets the devices you
  paired reach your Mac through your own VPN or a port you forward on your
  router; a device learns how the next time it connects at home with Remote
  Access on. A device away from home gets a quality of its own, Low at Standard
  resolution until you pick another there or in Sill's settings, so a slow
  connection never starts at your home quality; your home quality comes back
  as soon as a device at home connects. A device that reaches your Mac through
  a relay or tunnel running on the Mac itself, such as a userspace Tailscale
  node or an SSH tunnel, counts as away too. When your device comes home and your
  network lists your Mac, the session moves to your network by itself.
- **When the link can't keep up**, Sill for Mac notices that it is holding
  frames back and tells your device, which says so over the picture and, in
  its Settings, offers a quality the link can carry.
- **Text size**: Aa on your device resizes the window you stream, through
  Accessibility, so its text shows at the size you pick, and keeps it at that
  size while it streams, on the virtual display or, with that off, on your
  Mac's screen. The window goes back to its own size and place when Sill stops
  showing it: you pick another window or the Desktop, your last device
  disconnects, or you quit Sill. With the virtual display off, a window you
  moved on your Mac meanwhile keeps its new place, and Aa starts at Off, which
  leaves the window as it is: slide Aa back to Off and a window Sill resized
  goes back at once. Aa sizes a window, so it's dimmed while the Desktop shows.
- **The virtual display**, on unless you turn it off in the Sill menu or in
  Sill's Settings on your Mac, or in the settings panel of Sill on your iPhone
  or iPad, moves the window you stream onto a display of
  its own on your Mac, sized for your device, so it keeps updating when other
  windows cover it. The window leaves your Mac's screen while it streams and
  comes back where it was. The display uses a private macOS API, which is one
  reason Sill for Mac comes from the website and not from the Mac App Store; if
  a macOS update breaks it, Sill streams the window where it is.

Good to know: Sill shows one window, or the whole desktop, at a time, and it
plays your Mac's sound on your device as a beta, on by default. While the
virtual display is on, the window your device shows isn't on your Mac's screen
until you stop. The clipboard carries text only, up to 256 KB at a time, and
only between apps that both have it. Your Mac needs to be awake, with Sill
open. Sill may not be able to wake it. After a restart Sill opens only once
someone logs in, with Launch at Login on.
Only the iPhones and iPads you paired can connect, unless you turn off Require
pairing in Settings › Devices; then any device on your network can, still
encrypted. Pairing at home came with Sill for Mac 0.4.0 and Sill for iPhone and
iPad 0.5 (2), and each needs the other: the iPhone and iPad app shows an older
Sill for Mac as "Update Sill", and an older iPhone and iPad app can't connect
to Sill for Mac 0.4.0 or later at home. Since 0.5.1 the two apps share one
version number for each release. With Sill for Mac 0.3.1 or earlier,
connections on your local network, over the cable and over Direct Wireless
Connection are not encrypted, and anything that reaches your Mac there can
connect without pairing: update it.
Nightly builds: every night main changes, a notarized Sill for Mac built from it
goes to the [nightly pre-release](https://github.com/Saffsanity/sill/releases/tag/nightly),
and Sill for iPhone and iPad to TestFlight's testers. A nightly is tested less
than a release and can break, and going back from a nightly Sill for Mac to the
release keeps its settings and paired devices.
Or turn on Use nightly builds in Sill for Mac's Settings › General (0.6.2 or later): Sill then
offers each night's build too, built and signed by GitHub from Sill's newest code with nobody
looking at it first. A nightly installs only when you click Update Now; Automatically update Sill
installs releases only. A nightly is offered the release it led up to once that is out.

## Tips

Sill is free, with no ads, no tracking and no subscription. If it is useful to
you, a tip through [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/Saffsanity)
helps pay for the developer account. A tip unlocks nothing: every feature is
free. Who sponsors Sill, who has contributed, and how to join
them: [getsill.app/contribute](https://getsill.app/contribute).

## Building from source

You need a Mac with Xcode (Sill is built with Xcode 27; the iPhone and iPad
app needs Xcode 27.1 or later, for the iPhone Duo's hinge and fold), selected
as the active developer directory, with its license accepted.

Sill for Mac, from the repository's folder:

```
Scripts/make-app.sh --install --open
```

This builds Sill.app with SwiftPM, signs it with your Apple Development
identity, replaces /Applications/Sill.app and opens it. If that was the Sill
for Mac you downloaded, grant Screen Recording and Accessibility again and
pair each device again: the download keeps its key and paired devices in the
data-protection keychain, which only a Developer ID build with the project's
provisioning profile reads, and a build of your own keeps them in your login
keychain. Without `--install` it only builds `.build/Sill.app`. With no Apple
Development identity it signs ad hoc, and then Screen Recording and
Accessibility have to be granted again after every build.

For work on the host itself, `swift run -c release SillHost` runs the same
host on the command line, with one difference: unless you add `--pairing`, its
home door is plain and open, with no pairing and no encryption, and any device
on your network can connect to it, so run it only while developing. The App
Store's Sill for iPhone and iPad never dials such a door ("Update Sill"); a
Debug build from this repository can ([docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md),
Pairing at home). With `--synthetic` it streams a test pattern with no Screen
Recording needed.

The iPhone and iPad app:

1. Open `iOSClient/Sill.xcodeproj`.
2. In the Sill target's Signing & Capabilities, pick your team, and change the
   bundle identifier `me.saffer.sill` to one of your own.
3. Run it on an iPhone or iPad on the same network as your Mac, and tap your
   Mac. The first time, a Sill for Mac built from this repository asks you to
   pair: scan the code it shows, or connect the device with a USB cable.

[docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) has the rest: every command-line
flag, the test tools and the simulator harness, permissions and how to reset
them, Remote Access, troubleshooting and releases.

## Contributing

Issues are welcome: bug reports, questions and ideas. For a pull request, keep
to the conventions and decisions in [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): Swift and Apple
frameworks only, no third-party dependencies, nothing that needs a server, and
latency before picture quality. Open an issue before starting anything large.
Before a pull request, `Tests/checks/run-all.sh` runs the same pure checks as
CI, in about five minutes and with no device.
Contributions are accepted under the project's license. Please report a
security problem privately, as [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) says, not in a
public issue. These rules, with the sponsors and the contributors, are at
[getsill.app/contribute](https://getsill.app/contribute).
